package_info.package_versions: All observed variants (multiple hashes, see IOCs)
package_info.why_malicious: The MetaStealer family consists of macOS application bundles containing heavily obfuscated Go-based executables designed to exfiltrate sensitive business data, including keychain and other credentials, to attacker-controlled infrastructure. The applications are distributed via social engineering, masquerading as legitimate business-related software, and contain only the minimal files required for a valid macOS app, with the main payload being a malicious Mach-O binary.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime (when the user launches the malicious app), the code accesses the macOS keychain and other sensitive business files, collects this data, and exfiltrates it via HTTPS POST to attacker-controlled infrastructure (api.osx-mac.com), resulting in credential and business data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing the keychain and exfiltrating its contents to an external server is a classic infostealer behavior and is never expected from legitimate business applications.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal macOS business apps do not access or exfiltrate keychain data or sensitive business documents without explicit user consent and clear business justification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate backup or migration tools may access keychain data, but only with explicit user permission and never exfiltrate it to unknown servers.
key_indicators: Network communication to hardcoded C2 domains (api.osx-mac.com)
Collection and exfiltration of business documents

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends collected sensitive data to a hardcoded C2 endpoint (api.osx-mac.com) via HTTPS POST, enabling remote exfiltration of stolen information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hardcoded C2 endpoints and exfiltration of sensitive data are hallmarks of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications do not send sensitive user or business data to unknown external servers without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise apps may upload data to trusted cloud endpoints, but never to untrusted or unknown domains.
key_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST with sensitive payload

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code searches the filesystem for business-related documents (e.g., PDFs, contracts, agreements), collects them, and prepares them for exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unprompted enumeration and collection of business documents is a clear sign of data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate business apps do not indiscriminately search for and collect sensitive documents without user direction.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Document management tools may index files, but with user awareness and for local use only.
key_indicators: Automated search for business-sensitive file types

attack_chain.action: Victim is socially engineered to download and open a malicious .dmg or .zip containing a disguised business app.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the malicious Mach-O binary

attack_chain.action: Malicious Mach-O binary is executed, initiating infostealer logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of keychain and business documents

attack_chain.action: Collected keychain data and business documents are exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive data for further exploitation

behavioral_signatures: macOS application bundles with minimal structure and obfuscated Go-based Mach-O binaries
Access to keychain data or sensitive business files without user interaction
Outbound network connections to hardcoded, suspicious domains (e.g., api.osx-mac.com)
Collection and exfiltration of business documents at runtime
file_indicators: Disk images (.dmg) and zip files with business-themed names (e.g., 'AdobeOfficialBriefDescription.dmg', 'OfficialBriefDescription.app.zip')
Mach-O binaries with SHA-256 hashes as listed in IOCs
Application bundles with only Info.plist, Resources/icon, and MacOS/<executable>
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of unsigned or minimally structured macOS application bundles containing obfuscated Go-based Mach-O binaries, especially those distributed via disk images or zip files with business-related names. Alert on processes accessing the keychain or searching for business documents without user interaction, and on outbound network connections to known MetaStealer C2 domains or IPs. Correlate file hashes and bundle structures with published IOCs.
